issues.legal_issue: A claim concerning rights in property subject to statutory secured-creditor enforcement cannot be diverted to a separate civil forum when the matter falls within the jurisdiction of the specialist recovery tribunals.
material_facts: A bank had initiated statutory enforcement against a flat mortgaged as security for a company’s debt.
People claiming rights in the flat sought to restrain its auction, relying on an unregistered memorandum of understanding and other documents.
The recovery tribunal and appellate tribunal found that the mortgage was validly created and that the claimants had not established a subsisting interest in the flat.
The High Court did not assess those concurrent findings and instead gave the claimants liberty to approach another forum.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not give the claimants liberty to seek separate adjudication of their rights in the secured property; the statutory scheme bars civil-court proceedings on matters the recovery tribunals are empowered to determine and bars injunctions concerning enforcement under that scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13 and 34 of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 provide for enforcement of security interests and bar civil-court jurisdiction over matters that the Debts Recovery Tribunal or Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine; they also bar injunctions against action taken or to be taken under the Act. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: secured_enforcement_proceeding and tribunal_has_authority_over_dispute and claim_concerns_secured_property and high_court_authorizes_separate_civil_adjudication

predicates.secured_enforcement_proceeding: A creditor has initiated statutory enforcement against property securing a debt.
predicates.tribunal_has_authority_over_dispute: The dispute concerns a matter that a specialist recovery tribunal is empowered to determine.
predicates.claim_concerns_secured_property: A claimant asserts rights or interests in property being enforced against as security.
predicates.high_court_authorizes_separate_civil_adj: A High Court permits the claimant to pursue the property-rights dispute in a separate civil forum.

issues.definition: When statutory enforcement concerns secured property and the recovery tribunal has authority over the dispute, a High Court cannot authorize separate civil adjudication of a claim to that property.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not require a creditor to place money in an interest-bearing deposit for the benefit of whichever party later succeeds when that direction is uncalled for.
material_facts: The High Court directed the bank to deposit money in an interest-bearing account and provided that the proceeds would benefit the party successful in the litigation.
The bank challenged that direction in its appeal.
issues.conclusion: The direction requiring the bank to make the deposit was wholly uncalled for.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the deposit direction was wholly uncalled for; the judgment cites no provision or earlier case as the basis for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_challenges_high_court_order: A party appeals a High Court order.
predicates.high_court_orders_creditor_deposit_for_s: The High Court directs a creditor to place money in an interest-bearing deposit for the benefit of whichever party succeeds.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a High Court order that requires a creditor to make a deposit for the successful party, the deposit direction is uncalled for.

issues.legal_issue: When a High Court has not examined the merits of a challenge to tribunal findings, the appellate court may restore the proceeding for the High Court to decide while leaving the disputed questions open.
material_facts: The recovery tribunal and appellate tribunal had made concurrent findings against the claimants’ asserted interest in the secured property.
The High Court did not analyse those findings and disposed of the writ petition by allowing the claimants to seek relief in another forum.
The bank asked the Supreme Court to decide the merits, while the claimants argued that material matters had not been considered by the tribunals.
The Supreme Court declined to decide the merits, set aside the High Court judgment, and restored the writ petition for decision on its merits, leaving all questions open.
issues.conclusion: The writ petition was restored to the High Court for decision on its own merits and in accordance with law, with all questions left open.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered it appropriate to return the matter to the High Court because that court had not analysed the merits and the parties disputed whether material matters had been considered. The judgment relies on no provision or earlier case for this procedural disposition.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_disposition: A party appeals a High Court’s disposition of a writ proceeding.
predicates.high_court_did_not_analyse_merits: The High Court disposed of the proceeding without examining the merits of the tribunal’s findings.
predicates.material_disputes_remain_unresolved: The parties continue to dispute material matters relevant to the claim.

issues.definition: When a High Court has not examined the merits and material disputes remain unresolved, the proceeding may be restored for the High Court to decide those merits.
